title: High-content phenotyping of Parkinson's disease patient stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons using machine learning classification.
summary: The primary Results and Experimental Procedures show image-derived multivariate phenotypes and classifiers separated LRRK2-mutant from isogenic control dopaminergic neurons and detected compound effects, with a second SNCA triplication model used for validation.
ai_technology: Results and Experimental Procedures show image-derived multivariate phenotypes and classifiers separated LRRK2-mutant from isogenic control dopaminergic neurons and detected compound effects, with a second SNCA triplication model used for validation.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: LDA, SVM and LightGBM used quantitative image features; the paper applied the trained classifier to independent SNCA-triplication neurons and to treated versus DMSO neurons.
evidence.unknown: The isogenic and second-model comparisons support in-vitro disease-model phenotyping; this does not establish patient benefit or a new clinical therapy.
